title: [Text Extractor] Captures mirrored screen area (X-axis inversion) when Windows display language is Arabic (RTL)

judgment.rationale: The reporter supplied exact RTL steps plus a bugreport ZIP that confirms Arabic is the preferred Text Extractor language, and the current overlay converts logical selection coordinates to screen pixels separately from the capture path.
evidence: The report says selecting text on the right side of the screen captures OCR from the mirrored left side when Windows is Arabic/RTL.
The attached bugreport settings show PreferredLanguage set to Arabic.
OCROverlay.xaml.cs builds regionScaled from overlay coordinates and ImageMethods.GetRegionAsBitmap later offsets that region against the physical screen rectangle.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a design pass that normalizes overlay selection coordinates to physical screen coordinates and validate it with an Arabic-display repro.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing linked fix covers RTL coordinate normalization for Text Extractor capture rectangles.

issue_context.summary: Text Extractor highlights the correct RTL selection visually but appears to hand a mirrored X coordinate into the physical screen-capture step, so OCR receives pixels from the opposite side of the screen.
known_information: The report contains deterministic steps and names Arabic Windows display language as the trigger.
The bugreport ZIP confirms the preferred Text Extractor language is Arabic.
The attached Text Extractor logs show normal startup rather than a crash.
inferences: The failure is likely in coordinate conversion, not OCR language recognition itself.
The existing RTL text-reordering code in ImageMethods should stay separate from any fix.
issue_context.analysis: This is actionable because the owning code path is short and the bugreport confirms an RTL environment. The paired next step is a reproduce action, not another reporter ask.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the issue body and attached bugreport ZIP.
Read TextExtractor/settings.json from the ZIP and confirmed Arabic is the preferred language.
Reviewed OCROverlay.xaml.cs and ImageMethods.cs to trace overlay coordinates into screen capture.

comment.body: Approve a focused Text Extractor RTL coordinate-normalization design pass for Issue 50215.

actions.label: Reproduce Arabic RTL capture inversion
actions.note: Validate overlay-to-screen coordinate conversion under RTL display language.

reproduce.version: Preview v0.101.2373.0 or newer current main build
prerequisites: Set Windows display language to Arabic or another RTL language.
Enable Text Extractor and keep its activation shortcut available.
steps: Open Text Extractor in the RTL environment.
Drag a capture rectangle over text positioned on the right side of the screen.
Confirm whether the highlighted region and the OCR-captured pixels refer to the same on-screen location.
reproduce.expected_result: The OCR capture should come from the same right-side region that the overlay highlights, with no mirrored X-axis inversion.

proposed_fixes.title: Normalize Text Extractor selection rectangles before physical screen capture
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Text Extractor appears to draw the overlay selection in a UI context influenced by RTL layout while the actual screen capture uses physical left-to-right screen coordinates. The selected rectangle therefore needs to be normalized into physical monitor coordinates before ImageMethods copies pixels from the screen.
plan: Trace the overlay selection rectangle from OCROverlay to ImageMethods.GetRegionAsBitmap and define one canonical physical-coordinate representation.
Normalize the left/top calculation for RTL environments before the region is passed into screen capture.
Keep OCR text-order handling separate from capture-rectangle handling.
verification: Reproduce on an Arabic Windows display language and confirm the OCR region captures the same right-side pixels the overlay highlights.
Re-run an LTR capture to confirm the standard path does not regress.

confidence.rationale: The repro is concrete and the owning coordinate-conversion path is narrow, but the exact RTL boundary still needs validation.

design_decision.reason: Actionable design retained without full expansion.
